web_evidence.title: End of Watch by Stephen King – exclusive extract
web_evidence.note: A sustained extract reprinted by permission of Hodder & Stoughton narrates Holly and Hodges externally as she/he while moving between their thoughts; first-person forms are confined to dialogue or thought.

web_evidence.title: Stephen King Writing Styles in End of Watch
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies the novel's narrator as third-person omniscient and describes its shifts of focus among Brady, Hodges, and other characters.

search_log: Searched "Stephen King End of Watch official excerpt publisher" and "site:stephenking.com End of Watch excerpt"; found the authorized Guardian extract, publisher pages, and Stephen King's official pointer to an Entertainment Weekly excerpt.
Opened the Guardian extract and verified sustained third-person narration around Holly and Hodges; its permission statement establishes authorized excerpt status.

Searched "End of Watch Stephen King first chapter excerpt narrative point of view" and "End of Watch Stephen King third person present tense narrator"; found and opened BookRags' explicit whole-book point-of-view description.
Opened Simon & Schuster and Hachette UK publisher pages; their accessible text was synopsis/catalog material rather than diagnostic prose, so it was not used as person evidence.

Opened StephenKing.com's excerpt announcement, but it only linked to an external Entertainment Weekly page and contained no excerpt text; no credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections was found.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating third person, moving externally among Hodges, Holly, Brady, Rob, Jason, and others while sometimes reporting their thoughts. Multiple Goodreads event passages independently display this pattern, and the authorized interior extract matches it; the whole-book study guide explicitly calls the narrator third-person omniscient. Visible I/you forms occur in dialogue, direct thought, embedded reported speech, or maxims rather than autonomous base-narrative sections. Some quotes are too short or clipped to diagnose independently, but none supplies credible contrary structure. The evidence does not indicate sustained first- or second-person sections.
